facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus lived during the early Jurassic Period, specifically the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages.
facts.quote: Gongxianosaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur from the early Jurassic Period (Sinemurian-Pliensbachian stage).

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus lived approximately 183 to 174 million years ago during the Toarcian age.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 183 y 174 millones de años en el Toarciense

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus lived in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus fossils were discovered in May 1997 during a geological exploration.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in May 1997 during a geological exploration.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Gongxianosaurus was likely destroyed when the protective exhibition hall built over it collapsed.
facts.quote: The holotype of Gongxianosaurus was kept in situ and a protective exhibition hall was built over it. The exhibition hall subsequently collapsed, and the specimen was most likely destroyed.

facts.statement: Although Gongxianosaurus was named in 1998, a comprehensive scientific description has not yet been published.
facts.quote: Gongxianosaurus was firstly named and described in a short note published in 1998; however, a comprehensive description has yet to be published.

facts.statement: The known skeleton of Gongxianosaurus is largely complete but lacks the hands and most of the skull.
facts.quote: The skeleton is known in large part, missing both the hand and the majority of the skull.

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus may have reached a length of 14 meters.
facts.quote: Gongxianosaurus may have reached 14 m in length.

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus moved quadrupedally, with forelimbs reaching 70% to 75% of the hind limb length.
facts.quote: Like other sauropods, it moved quadrupedally (on four legs), as indicated by the elongated fore limbs that reached 70 to 75% of hind limb length.

facts.statement: Unlike other sauropods, Gongxianosaurus lacked pleurocoels, suggesting its vertebrae were quite massive.
facts.quote: Unlike in other sauropods, pleurocoels (deep lateral excavations of the vertebrae) were absent; thus, the vertebrae would have been quite massive.

facts.statement: The genus Gongxianosaurus was established by He et al. in 1998.
facts.quote: genus_authority: He et al, 1998

facts.statement: The species Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis was established by He et al. in 1998.
facts.quote: species_authority: He et al, 1998

facts.statement: It is debated whether some fossils belong to Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis or a second species, with Ouyang Hui informally naming the latter Yibinosaurus zhoui.
facts.quote: Luo and Wang suggest that several bones may not pertain to the type species Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis but to a second species of Gongxianosaurus. Those remains were informally placed within the separate genus and species "Yibinosaurus zhoui" in 2001 and 2003 respectively by Ouyang Hui.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Gongxianosaurus was one of the most basal sauropods or if ossified distal tarsals were present in other early sauropods but not preserved.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Gongxianosaurus fue uno de los saurópodos más bajos, o los tarsales distales osificados estaban presentes en otros saurópodos tempranos, pero simplemente no se conservan debido a lo pobre de los especímenes.

facts.statement: Remains of theropods were found alongside the Gongxianosaurus fossils.
facts.quote: While most fossils pertain to a new sauropod genus, remains of theropods have also been found.

facts.statement: The Gongxianosaurus material includes four individuals of similar size that encompass most of the skeleton, except for hand and skull bones, which are represented only by a premaxilla and teeth.
facts.quote: The sauropod material includes four fragmentary to complete individuals similar in size, together encompassing most of the skeleton, though hand and skull bones were not found except a premaxilla and teeth.

facts.statement: The pedal phalangeal formula of Gongxianosaurus is 2-3-4-5-1.
facts.quote: The pedal phalangeal formula, counting the number of phalanges for each digit starting from the innermost, was 2-3-4-5-1.

facts.statement: All digits of Gongxianosaurus except the outermost one ended in claws.
facts.quote: All but the outermost digit ended in claws.

facts.statement: The chevrons of Gongxianosaurus were unbifurcated.
facts.quote: The chevrons were unbifurcated.

facts.statement: Excavation of the Gongxianosaurus site recovered a wealth of fossils from an area of approximately 200 square meters.
facts.quote: Excavation started in the same month and led to the recovery of a wealth of fossils in an area of approximately 200 square meters.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses of Gongxianosaurus are limited because its fossils have not yet been fully described.
facts.quote: Debido a que los fósiles aún no están completamente descritos, la información de caracteres disponible que se puede usar en los análisis cladísticos es limitada.

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropodiformes.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropodiformes

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gongxianosaurus is Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis

facts.statement: Gongxianosaurus lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Gongxianosaurus was named by He and colleagues in 1998.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Gongxianosaurus (genus), He et al. 1998
